text.p: Blyth Industries Inc rose sharply Tuesday and a company spokeswoman said the increase might be attributed to short-covering by investors.

Shares in the Greenwich, Conn., maker of candles and fragrances items were up 4-1/2, or 11.39 percent, to 44-1/4 in early afternoon. Volume was 247,000 shares, well above the normal daily level of 136,000 shares.
Spokeswoman Jane Casey told Reuters the company had announced no news and the rise could be caused by investors buying shares to cover short positions.
"There is a large short position" of 3.2 million shares, she said. The company has about 31.4 million outstanding.
"I suspect that somebody decided to start ... a kind of short-covering type of situation."
Tom O'Halloran, an analyst at Dillon Read, said the stock had suffered a "nasty correction," falling from 51 in July 1996 to 31-1/2 in April.
"It just seems to be rallying out of an oversold position," he said.
O'Halloran expected Blyth to report good results when it releases fiscal first quarter earnings June 3.
The consensus estimate for earnings per share for the quarter, which ends April 30, is $0.30 against $0.23 for the same period a year ago.
